While the extra cost was obvious, I planned to use it for a long time, and I knew I'd be bothered if I didn't do this every day. Ultimately, I'm satisfied with the result. It's convenient to store dishes, dispose of food waste, and remove any remaining residue before putting them away. While comparing models, I had a thought about why there was so much moisture in my previous review when there was a drying function. After using it myself, I'll tell you the result. However, if you use the strong drying function, there is almost no moisture! (). The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. Product name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Kitchen Fit Built-in Dishwasher for 14 People [DW60BB800ULWS]. Color: Glam White. Installation method: Built-in installation. Country of manufacture: Thailand. Manufacturer/importer: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. Release date of the same model: January 2023. [Main functions]. Sterilization + drying (not 100 degree hot air drying). Automatic door opening function. Washing performance: 4-stage 3D water flow / 720 degree moving washing wing (bottom) / Wide washing wing (top) / No AI customized washing. Included high-temperature direct water washing / No water filter. Number of dish baskets: 3 EA / No internal lighting. ********( . )******* . Hello. First of all, I often have meals with my two sons, aged 3 and 5, my husband, and my in-laws. Because of this, I had a lot of dishes to wash, and I was stuck in dishwashing hell for over five years after getting married. Then, suddenly, I received a new dishwasher, and after meticulously researching and comparing prices for over a month, I finally decided to bring my aunt in. I searched YouTube and looked at three popular brands, comparing prices daily, and finally settled on this one. I also consulted with other moms and compared their opinions. All the manufacturers had hot air dryers, and they were even more expensive. The reason I omitted this feature was because washing dishes in extremely hot water was impossible, and even without the hot air dryer, it still had the ability to wash and dry at temperatures above 75 degrees Celsius. My children had already grown out of bottles, so I didn't think this feature was absolutely necessary, so I decided to focus on cost-effectiveness. ( _). So, while comparing 12-seater models, I saw this Samsung model listed at a lower price than other 12-seater models. The 14-seater model also held 16 more dishes, which was tempting. This finally put an end to my worries. The product in question was a relatively new model, released in January 2023, and I compared its performance with that of the 14-person model. The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. Regarding the purified water washing function, since I usually wash dishes with tap water instead of purified water, and since my house doesn't have groundwater, I figured it was fine. When comparing, AI is convenient! I think you can compare prices by saying things like, "I find it annoying," "It's a waste of electricity to leave the light on at night," and "I feel more secure washing with purified water." I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. However, when comparing with other brands, I found that all of them exhibited the same symptoms and attributed it to the typical dishwasher drying process. In fact, I didn't find it particularly unpleasant (since it's not constantly next to the dishwasher). ()*:.. .:**. One difference from other brands is that Samsung takes two days to install. They first check the proper installation location, and then the installer comes the next day to quickly complete the installation. It took a total of 50 minutes + 30 minutes (-). I moved the dishwasher next to the sink to make it easier to move dishes around. While the extra cost was obvious, I planned to use it for a long time, and I knew I'd be bothered if I didn't do this every day. Ultimately, I'm satisfied with the result. It's convenient to store dishes, dispose of food waste, and remove any remaining residue before putting them away. While comparing models, I had a thought about why there was so much moisture in my previous review when there was a drying function. After using it myself, I'll tell you the result. If you wash in standard mode and don't use the separate strong drying function, there is a lot of moisture as you can see in the attached photo on the door. However, if you use the strong drying function, there is almost no moisture! (). Ultimately, I'm so happy to have escaped the dishwashing hell, and although housework hasn't completely disappeared, considering the time it takes to put away after applying detergent, rinsing, and drying, I highly recommend it to those who didn't have a dishwasher. There's a lot more I could explain, but this is already too long, so I'll stop here. I'm very satisfied with this product and am using it. I hope you found my review helpful! Sterilization + drying (not 100 degree hot air drying). Automatic door opening function. Washing performance: 4-stage 3D water flow / 720 degree moving washing wing (bottom) / Wide washing wing (top) / No AI customized washing. Included high-temperature direct water washing / No water filter. Number of dish baskets: 3 EA / No internal lighting. ********( . )******* . Hello. First of all, I often have meals with my two sons, aged 3 and 5, my husband, and my in-laws. Because of this, I had a lot of dishes to wash, and I was stuck in dishwashing hell for over five years after getting married. Then, suddenly, I received a new dishwasher, and after meticulously researching and comparing prices for over a month, I finally decided to bring my aunt in. I searched YouTube and looked at three popular brands, comparing prices daily, and finally settled on this one. I also consulted with other moms and compared their opinions. All the manufacturers had hot air dryers, and they were even more expensive. The reason I omitted this feature was because washing dishes in extremely hot water was impossible, and even without the hot air dryer, it still had the ability to wash and dry at temperatures above 75 degrees Celsius. My children had already grown out of bottles, so I didn't think this feature was absolutely necessary, so I decided to focus on cost-effectiveness. ( _). So, while comparing 12-seater models, I saw this Samsung model listed at a lower price than other 12-seater models. The 14-seater model also held 16 more dishes, which was tempting. This finally put an end to my worries. The product in question was a relatively new model, released in January 2023, and I compared its performance with that of the 14-person model. The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. Regarding the purified water washing function, since I usually wash dishes with tap water instead of purified water, and since my house doesn't have groundwater, I figured it was fine. When comparing, AI is convenient! I think you can compare prices by saying things like, "I find it annoying," "It's a waste of electricity to leave the light on at night," and "I feel more secure washing with purified water." I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. However, when comparing with other brands, I found that all of them exhibited the same symptoms and attributed it to the typical dishwasher drying process. In fact, I didn't find it particularly unpleasant (since it's not constantly next to the dishwasher). ()*:.. .:**. One difference from other brands is that Samsung takes two days to install. They first check the proper installation location, and then the installer comes the next day to quickly complete the installation. It took a total of 50 minutes + 30 minutes (-). I moved the dishwasher next to the sink to make it easier to move dishes around. While the extra cost was obvious, I planned to use it for a long time, and I knew I'd be bothered if I didn't do this every day. Ultimately, I'm satisfied with the result. It's convenient to store dishes, dispose of food waste, and remove any remaining residue before putting them away. While comparing models, I had a thought about why there was so much moisture in my previous review when there was a drying function. After using it myself, I'll tell you the result. If you wash in standard mode and don't use the separate strong drying function, there is a lot of moisture as you can see in the attached photo on the door. However, if you use the strong drying function, there is almost no moisture! (). Ultimately, I'm so happy to have escaped the dishwashing hell, and although housework hasn't completely disappeared, considering the time it takes to put away after applying detergent, rinsing, and drying, I highly recommend it to those who didn't have a dishwasher. There's a lot more I could explain, but this is already too long, so I'll stop here. I'm very satisfied with this product and am using it. I hope you found my review helpful! Comments (English): [ Dishwasher purchase increases happiness index! ] || ---------------- || This is a review of a purchase I made with my own money. Product name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Kitchen Fit Built-in Dishwasher for 14 People [DW60BB800ULWS]. Color: Glam White. Installation method: Built-in installation. Country of manufacture: Thailand. Manufacturer/importer: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. Release date of the same model: January 2023. [Main functions]. Sterilization + drying (not 100 degree hot air drying). Automatic door opening function. Washing performance: 4-stage 3D water flow / 720 degree moving washing wing (bottom) / Wide washing wing (top) / No AI customized washing. Included high-temperature direct water washing / No water filter. Number of dish baskets: 3 EA / No internal lighting. ********( . )******* . Hello. First of all, I often have meals with my two sons, aged 3 and 5, my husband, and my in-laws. Because of this, I had a lot of dishes to wash, and I was stuck in dishwashing hell for over five years after getting married. Then, suddenly, I received a new dishwasher, and after meticulously researching and comparing prices for over a month, I finally decided to bring my aunt in. I searched YouTube and looked at three popular brands, comparing prices daily, and finally settled on this one. I also consulted with other moms and compared their opinions. All the manufacturers had hot air dryers, and they were even more expensive. The reason I omitted this feature was because washing dishes in extremely hot water was impossible, and even without the hot air dryer, it still had the ability to wash and dry at temperatures above 75 degrees Celsius. My children had already grown out of bottles, so I didn't think this feature was absolutely necessary, so I decided to focus on cost-effectiveness. ( _). So, while comparing 12-seater models, I saw this Samsung model listed at a lower price than other 12-seater models. The 14-seater model also held 16 more dishes, which was tempting. This finally put an end to my worries. The product in question was a relatively new model, released in January 2023, and I compared its performance with that of the 14-person model. The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. Regarding the purified water washing function, since I usually wash dishes with tap water instead of purified water, and since my house doesn't have groundwater, I figured it was fine. When comparing, AI is convenient! I think you can compare prices by saying things like, "I find it annoying," "It's a waste of electricity to leave the light on at night," and "I feel more secure washing with purified water." I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. However, when comparing with other brands, I found that all of them exhibited the same symptoms and attributed it to the typical dishwasher drying process. In fact, I didn't find it particularly unpleasant (since it's not constantly next to the dishwasher). ()*:.. .:**. One difference from other brands is that Samsung takes two days to install. They first check the proper installation location, and then the installer comes the next day to quickly complete the installation. It took a total of 50 minutes + 30 minutes (-). I moved the dishwasher next to the sink to make it easier to move dishes around. While the extra cost was obvious, I planned to use it for a long time, and I knew I'd be bothered if I didn't do this every day. Ultimately, I'm satisfied with the result. It's convenient to store dishes, dispose of food waste, and remove any remaining residue before putting them away. While comparing models, I had a thought about why there was so much moisture in my previous review when there was a drying function. After using it myself, I'll tell you the result. If you wash in standard mode and don't use the separate strong drying function, there is a lot of moisture as you can see in the attached photo on the door. However, if you use the strong drying function, there is almost no moisture! (). Ultimately, I'm so happy to have escaped the dishwashing hell, and although housework hasn't completely disappeared, considering the time it takes to put away after applying detergent, rinsing, and drying, I highly recommend it to those who didn't have a dishwasher. There's a lot more I could explain, but this is already too long, so I'll stop here. I'm very satisfied with this product and am using it. I hope you found my review helpful! Sterilization + drying (not 100 degree hot air drying). Automatic door opening function. Included high-temperature direct water washing / No water filter. Number of dish baskets: 3 EA / No internal lighting. ********( . )******* . Hello. First of all, I often have meals with my two sons, aged 3 and 5, my husband, and my in-laws. Because of this, I had a lot of dishes to wash, and I was stuck in dishwashing hell for over five years after getting married. Then, suddenly, I received a new dishwasher, and after meticulously researching and comparing prices for over a month, I finally decided to bring my aunt in. I searched YouTube and looked at three popular brands, comparing prices daily, and finally settled on this one. I also consulted with other moms and compared their opinions. All the manufacturers had hot air dryers, and they were even more expensive. The reason I omitted this feature was because washing dishes in extremely hot water was impossible, and even without the hot air dryer, it still had the ability to wash and dry at temperatures above 75 degrees Celsius. My children had already grown out of bottles, so I didn't think this feature was absolutely necessary, so I decided to focus on cost-effectiveness. ( _). So, while comparing 12-seater models, I saw this Samsung model listed at a lower price than other 12-seater models. The 14-seater model also held 16 more dishes, which was tempting. This finally put an end to my worries. The product in question was a relatively new model, released in January 2023, and I compared its performance with that of the 14-person model. The key features upgraded from the 14-person model were the AI mode and the interior lighting for nighttime use! The only difference was the filtering and cleaning functions. I decided I could probably do without these three items. I use a Samsung washer/dryer, and I find the AI function useful in the dryer. It saves me a lot of thinking! It does everything for me. ( ). However, I thought I could choose the dishwashing mode based on the amount of dishes I had that day. I didn't really need the lighting after I finished washing the dishes at night, so I figured I could just turn it on. Regarding the purified water washing function, since I usually wash dishes with tap water instead of purified water, and since my house doesn't have groundwater, I figured it was fine. When comparing, AI is convenient! I think you can compare prices by saying things like, "I find it annoying," "It's a waste of electricity to leave the light on at night," and "I feel more secure washing with purified water." I've also seen reviews that say the dryer generates heat and can produce a slight odor. However, when comparing with other brands, I found that all of them exhibited the same symptoms and attributed it to the typical dishwasher drying process. In fact, I didn't find it particularly unpleasant (since it's not constantly next to the dishwasher). ()*:.. .:**. One difference from other brands is that Samsung takes two days to install. They first check the proper installation location, and then the installer comes the next day to quickly complete the installation. It took a total of 50 minutes + 30 minutes (-). I moved the dishwasher next to the sink to make it easier to move dishes around. While the extra cost was obvious, I planned to use it for a long time, and I knew I'd be bothered if I didn't do this every day. Ultimately, I'm satisfied with the result. It's convenient to store dishes, dispose of food waste, and remove any remaining residue before putting them away. While comparing models, I had a thought about why there was so much moisture in my previous review when there was a drying function. After using it myself, I'll tell you the result. If you wash in standard mode and don't use the separate strong drying function, there is a lot of moisture as you can see in the attached photo on the door. However, if you use the strong drying function, there is almost no moisture! (). Ultimately, I'm so happy to have escaped the dishwashing hell, and although housework hasn't completely disappeared, considering the time it takes to put away after applying detergent, rinsing, and drying, I highly recommend it to those who didn't have a dishwasher. There's a lot more I could explain, but this is already too long, so I'll stop here. I'm very satisfied with this product and am using it. I hope you found my review helpful! In fact, it's level of quietness was unheard of in dishwashers under $1,000 - at least back in 2020. It is quite the gut-punch to have to replace a major appliance after only 3-1/2 years, so this time I am going with Bosch, which ranks high in terms of long-term reliability.

Sentence (English): We purchased our Samsung DW80R9950US in December of 2020, and by May of 2024 (3-1/2 years later), we are replacing it.
Comments (English): [ Seals and Motor Failed After Only 3-1/2 Years! ] || ---------------- || We purchased our Samsung DW80R9950US in December of 2020, and by May of 2024 (3-1/2 years later), we are replacing it. The seals that protect the linear "waterwall" motor were leaking and caused corrosion on the motor, which eventually failed. At first, items in the bottom rack were not getting clean, and then the dishwasher simply would not start at all. We thought about repairing the dishwasher, but replacing seals that failed only after 3 years did not seem like a good idea. Our kitchen has a hardwood floor, and we feared subsequent seal failure could cause costly damage. When it comes to dishwasher reliability, Samsung has one of the worst reputations - as assessment back by Consumer Reports and by reviews on many other sites. We have other Samsung appliances (TV's, refrigerator), which are doing very well. When this dishwasher was functioning, it performed very well in terms of cleaning and quietness (38 dB). In fact, it's level of quietness was unheard of in dishwashers under $1,000 - at least back in 2020. It is quite the gut-punch to have to replace a major appliance after only 3-1/2 years, so this time I am going with Bosch, which ranks high in terms of long-term reliability.

Pros: the price is reasonable, the third rack is handy. Cons: It is rated as using more energy than my old one, there are less slots in the silverware basket (canceling out the advantage of a 3rd rack), and I HATE that it does not have a rinse and hold cycle, it has a rinse and wash later. Sentence (English): Positives: Quiet, and Quality Build, Warranty+Standard wash cycle is 2- 2.5 hours.
Comments (English): [ The tines they are a changin' ] || ---------------- || Positives: Quiet, and Quality Build, Warranty+Standard wash cycle is 2- 2.5 hours. +Can range from 70 mins Quick Wash without dry, to 3 hours deep wash depending on your preferences. +We love having a quiet unit. (Also noisy motors tend to not last as long.) Works well in an open configuration home. Would not interfere with dinner conversation even in the same room. +The volume of the beep at completion of wash can be adjusted up or down to just barely audible (or silenced), which is nice if you're relaxing after eating.+Top control gives the exterior a nice clean look, however there's no way to see the wash cycle progress. If you want to change a control you will have to interrupt a cycle and open the door. +It does not leak if opened mid-cycle.+You can see the wash completion by seeing a little red light reflected onto the floor. Subtle and not obtrusive.+It has a tine configuration for holding the stems of wine glasses, which is nifty.+We have fairly hard water but spots on glass don't seem to be very noticeable, even without using rinse aid. A rinse aid sample is included so you can test it out.Shortcomings:-Changing most of the wash selections from the previous wash is not intuitive. Usually have to reset the machine just to change one option.-Overall, the placement of the tines are NOT as well laid out as our previous Bosch. Or, frankly, any other dishwasher we've ever used. The awkward angling of the tines seems to result in wasted loading space.-Some items at the corners don't get washed enough. Workaround is we end up using those areas for our water glasses. -Detergent compartment is angled dramatically at the bottom. Perhaps so gel packs will slide out, but we use powder and it's a little tricky to gauge. It's just a minor thing. The good thing is that powder doesn't clump up as long as you pour it neatly into the compartment and not the conduit that releases the spring door. : )-Despite having a nice red LED display was surprised that it neither displays minutes remaining in cycle nor minutes to wash completion.-The dry function is inadequate. It's more like a steam room. We leave it the unit open overnight after the wash ends and are happy to get the moisture in our home, so I didn't take off for this because I consider it energy saving. There is an Extra Dry function for those who want it. As with all dishwashers, it would generate more heat of course.-Also keep in mind the third rack (at the top) does not actually receive water spray. This is beause there's no spray spinner dedicated to it. (The 2 spray spinners in the unit are designed to spray underneath the lower and middle racks.) It can only accomodate items about 1" high. So, good use of this space is for items that are basically clean but you want sanitized. Because they'll go through the high heat process but not get rinsed. The tradeoff of the top rack is that it takes up vertical space. In other words items more than about 7" high can't fit on the middle rack. I'd have preferred no third rack so we could wash more taller items.

The good thing is that powder doesn't clump up as long as you pour it neatly into the compartment and not the conduit that releases the spring door. : )-Despite having a nice red LED display was surprised that it neither displays minutes remaining in cycle nor minutes to wash completion.-The dry function is inadequate. It's more like a steam room. We leave it the unit open overnight after the wash ends and are happy to get the moisture in our home, so I didn't take off for this because I consider it energy saving. There is an Extra Dry function for those who want it. As with all dishwashers, it would generate more heat of course.-Also keep in mind the third rack (at the top) does not actually receive water spray. I'd have preferred no third rack so we could wash more taller items.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is fine except for a major, major design flaw with its buttons.
Comments (English): [ Terrible Button Design ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is fine except for a major, major design flaw with its buttons. They're front-facing and touch-sensitive, and they activate on ANY touch. If you're like us, your dishwasher area isn't deep enough to install it so that the counter hangs over the top; the front of the dishwasher is more EVEN with the counter, and that means that every time you work on the counter, you press against the buttons AND THEY ACTIVATE. Which means playing music. Our kitchen happens to have its primary workspace above the dishwasher, so every time we're using a cutting board or doing other work, we're activating that infernal music over and over again just by brushing against the dishwasher. This would not be a problem if the buttons were a different style or they were on the top instead of the front, but there's no solution for us. We can't push the dishwasher any further under the countertop; it's flush with the back wall.

Sentence (English): Generally satisfied with the unit but a couple of things are unhelpful.
Comments (English): [ A Couple of Issues ] || ---------------- || Generally satisfied with the unit but a couple of things are unhelpful. The third level utensil rack is oddly designed. It does not hold flatware in place. The pieces tip and move around when the drawer is pulled out, as one does when adding pieces between washes. It requires careful alignment of the pieces right before starting the unit. Because we own a Bosch DW with a third level rack in another residence, I know that the design of that rack can be much better. Additionally, the Normal cycle seems unnecessarily long: over 2 hours. The Express cycle is shorter but does not dry well. Finally, the vent in the door collects condensation during a wash, and that water drips onto the floor when the door is opened. Since installation about 3 weeks ago, I now know to use a towel to absorb the moisture before opening the door.

Sentence (English): This is my first dishwasher.
Comments (English): This is my first dishwasher. I am a single-person household, but I bought the biggest one. Do I cook a lot? No. But sometimes when I do, there are a lot of big pots and dishes, and I thought the 6-person one would be too small. I bought the latest model, thinking that I would rather buy a slightly bigger one than the 12-person one, and I am satisfied. The shelf height adjustment function and the touch panel on the top were also factors in my choice. Since it was my first time using it, it took me a while to put dishes on the rack, and I read the manual carefully because of the salt, detergent, and rinse. Of course, the installer explained everything in detail, but I moved in a week after the installation. Anyway, after experiencing the awkwardness and inconvenience of using it for the first time a few times, it is now very natural and comfortable. The design is also pretty. Sentence (English): I did a lot of research on the best bang for the $ before purchasing and Costco had a nice sale.
Comments (English): [ So far, so good.  ] || ---------------- || I did a lot of research on the best bang for the $ before purchasing and Costco had a nice sale. The dishwasher looks very high-end and sleek. I like the clean front with no badging. The controls are simple and to the point and it has all the features we needed, without the fluff. The capacity only states 13 place settings, but it holds more than our last GE Profile rated at 16 place settings. The top 3rd rack has minimal utility given the space and things in this rack don't get very dry, but the lower 2 racks do get quite dry, minus some typical puddling on the tops of cups. When unloading, start from the bottom and then middle rack so you don't splash them from the items on the 3rd rack. The 3rd rack is still handy though and there is plenty of height on the bottom 2 main racks for tall cups, pans, bowls etc (they sit a little lower than the last dishwasher). It is quiet enough to not really notice while watching TV in our family room, which is open to the kitchen. I will note too that I was worried about the install given some of the reviews. I'm in the DFW area and Ken's Appliance was who delivered and installed it for Costco. They did an excellent job. The 2 guys were quick, friendly, informative, very polite and everything works as intended, with no leaks.

Sentence (English): We've had our SHPM65Z55N/20 for about a year, having purchased it from a home improvement store on Consumer Reports' recommendation.
Comments (English): [ Not very good ] || ---------------- || We've had our SHPM65Z55N/20 for about a year, having purchased it from a home improvement store on Consumer Reports' recommendation. The machine is very quiet. If the bath fan down the hall is on, you have to look for the red light shining on the floor to know if the dishwasher is running. I expected it to wash better. The old cheap noisy one it replaced got dishes cleaner. Wash cycle is a little under 3 hours by default and a little over 3 hours if you want it to pop the door open when it's done. On about half of the loads it will stop mid-cycle. It indicates this by blinking the red light it shines on the floor. It doesn't provide any information about why it has stopped. It then needs someone to open the door and press start. Sometimes it then finishes washing, but more often it will continue to stop sporadically during the remainder of the ~3 hour cycle. Only rarely will it show an error code. The controls seem to be prone to becoming confused. If you press the buttons too quickly or in an unexpected order, it will fail to start the cycle. You might think that resetting the controls would require just holding the "reset" button, but really it seems to require holding "reset", turning off power, closing the door, and re-opening the door. Once you've done that, you can (slowly and deliberately so it doesn't get confused again! ) press Power, Auto Air, Start, close the door, and it will now run until it stops. Unless quietness is the only thing that matters to you, buy something else.

The machine is very quiet. If the bath fan down the hall is on, you have to look for the red light shining on the floor to know if the dishwasher is running. I expected it to wash better. The old cheap noisy one it replaced got dishes cleaner. Wash cycle is a little under 3 hours by default and a little over 3 hours if you want it to pop the door open when it's done. On about half of the loads it will stop mid-cycle. It indicates this by blinking the red light it shines on the floor. It doesn't provide any information about why it has stopped. It then needs someone to open the door and press start. Sometimes it then finishes washing, but more often it will continue to stop sporadically during the remainder of the ~3 hour cycle. Only rarely will it show an error code. The controls seem to be prone to becoming confused. If you press the buttons too quickly or in an unexpected order, it will fail to start the cycle. You might think that resetting the controls would require just holding the "reset" button, but really it seems to require holding "reset", turning off power, closing the door, and re-opening the door. Once you've done that, you can (slowly and deliberately so it doesn't get confused again! ) press Power, Auto Air, Start, close the door, and it will now run until it stops. Unless quietness is the only thing that matters to you, buy something else.

Sentence (English): I'm sorry to say that if there is one purchase choice I wish I could go back in time and reverse, it would be this one.
Comments (English): [ Worst appliance choice I've ever made ] || ---------------- || I'm sorry to say that if there is one purchase choice I wish I could go back in time and reverse, it would be this one. The TL;DR is that it only works intermittently, and so we are stuck with a decision of whether to be frustrated every single day, not knowing if it will decide to work, or dropping more money on a new dishwasher.First, just to be fair, the good: it really is quiet, is relatively easy to load and does a really good job of cleaning without requiring a lot of pre-rinsing.The bad: The machine simply isn't built well; it feels like a lower end Whirlpool with new badging. Honestly, I wish I'd been willing to spend a few hundred more dollars for a higher quality machine that wasn't so compromised or even spend twice as much for a Miele; but this one matched our other KitchenAid appliances, and we've been more than happy with them.The quality issues started with installation and is a good example of cost control oriented compromised design decisions KitchenAid made: the input coupling for the dishwasher is made of plastic (! ) not brass. This makes it very easy to misthread or not get a good connection even when properly threaded. I spent the first year with this machine just trying to get it to stop leaking. Why would they save a few bucks on such a critical part? And parts started breaking. Little parts are cheaply made and just not designed to withstand the rigors of a family using it day to day. Within a month, one of the plastic wheels for the rack broke, meaning that it doesn't open properly and every time we open the top rack it droops, and actually falls out of the guide if we pull it out to far. A reminder every time we load it of the poor decision we made.The worst: about a year in, the start button began to take short vacations, and over time those vacations have become more and more frequent. After consulting the internet, we discovered a fix that works about half of the time (and with a lower probability every day); cycling the power off and back on. Since the electrical connection isn't accessible, this means that every night after loading the dishwasher, we need to run down to the basement, flip the breaker, wait ten minutes, go bad down and turn it back on. Half the time that doesn't work, meaning we have to *unload* the dishwasher and hand wash everything.The only solution I can find is to replace the entire front panel, which is close to $500. I'm pretty handy with appliances -- I've kept our washing machine working for fifteen years, replacing every part that has broken to the point where the only thing that is original is the cabinet and controls. The reason I've kept it so long? Because it doesn't have any chips to control it; it's all relays and mechanical controls. The electronics are always the most expensive things to replace, and I'm not willing to go this route because it's almost half of what we payed for the dishwasher and I'm not at all confident something else won't break or I won't be replacing the same part in another couple of years.You can imagine that this experience has soured us on KitchenAid projects. Literally every day we are forced to spend anywhere from 10-45 minutes managing these failures. And this is supposed to be a time _saving_ product?

Sentence (English): Our 40 year old dishwasher died so we travelled to bestbuy to get another.
Comments (English): [ Decent option with lots of features ] || ---------------- || Our 40 year old dishwasher died so we travelled to Best Buy to get another. We are Total members, so it's worth it to us for the added warranty we get through the Total program to purchase through Best Buy.Dishwasher does a good job cleaning. You have the option to control the power of the wash by zones, which is cool if you have pots and pans to wash. The racks that hold the items are all slanted, which sometimes makes it difficult to load the dishwasher with items that do not fit into those rack spaces like mixing bowls or larger storage containers.This dishwasher is very quiet. They have an LED light that shines on the floor to let you know the dishwasher is working. Unless water is draining out into the sink drain, I would have no idea it was even running. The one big negative is the drying capabilities. If you run the normal program, the dishwasher doesn't use heat to dry. The inside of the dishwasher is stainless, and it cools off quicker than the dishes so the condensate forms on the side walls and runs down to drain out. This is okay for anything not plastic, but in our experience anything on the 3rd row is completely wet when the cycle ends (about 2.5 hrs), and anything plastic is still wet. We've tried everything we can, including selecting "Sanitize" function, but I would still say it's not great. It's tough to wait 2.5 hours and still have to dry some of the items you're taking out.If the lack of drying doesn't bother you I would recommend getting the Bosch. Otherwise, I would lean towards Kitchenaid.

Sentence (English): We recently upgraded to this GE dishwasher and I gotta say, it's been a game-changer in our kitchen!
Comments (English): [ Impressive GE Dishwasher Delivers Clean and Dry Dishes ] || ---------------- || We recently upgraded to this GE dishwasher and I gotta say, it's been a game-changer in our kitchen! The installation process was surprisingly straightforward - with the help of the manual and a few YouTube tutorials, I was able to get it up and running myself. No need to call in the pros! One feature that really stands out is the Dry Boost Technology. It's amazing how much drier our dishes come out, especially those pesky plastic containers that always seem to hold onto water. No more hand-drying or letting them air out on the counter! The third rack is another favorite of mine. It's super versatile and offers extra space for all those odd-shaped utensils and serving pieces. Plus, the adjustable upper rack makes it easy to fit taller items like wine glasses or oversized plates. Talk about flexibility! The bottle wash jets are a nice touch too. We have a lot of reusable water bottles and travel mugs, and these jets make sure they get a thorough clean every time. No more struggling to scrub the bottom of a narrow bottle by hand! I love the steam and sanitize option for those extra grimy loads. It gives me peace of mind knowing that everything is not only clean but also sanitized. And the 1-hour wash cycle is clutch when we're in a rush and need clean dishes ASAP.The AutoSense feature is pretty nifty - it adjusts the wash settings based on how dirty the dishes are, so we're not wasting water or energy on a light load. And the Wash Zones option lets us do a true half-load when we don't have a full dishwasher, saving even more resources.The Piranha hard food disposer is a lifesaver too. We can skip the pre-rinse and let the dishwasher handle even the toughest stuck-on food. No more elbow grease required! The capacity is impressive - we can fit a ton of dishes in there, even after a big family dinner. And the 47 dBA rating means it's whisper-quiet, so we can run it anytime without disrupting our daily life.The only minor drawback we've noticed is that sometimes the detergent dispenser doesn't open fully, leaving a bit of soap residue on the door. But it's rare and hasn't impacted the overall cleaning performance.We haven't splurged on the optional WiFi adapter yet, but it's nice to know we have that option for even more convenience down the line.After putting this dishwasher through its paces for a few weeks, we couldn't be happier with our choice. It delivers sparkling clean and dry dishes every time, and the thoughtful features make it a joy to use. If you're in the market for a reliable, high-performing dishwasher, this GE model is definitely worth considering! ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Sentence (English): Our 40 year old dishwasher died so we travelled to bestbuy to get another.
Comments (English): [ Decent option with lots of features ] || ---------------- || Our 40 year old dishwasher died so we travelled to Best Buy to get another. We are Total members, so it's worth it to us for the added warranty we get through the Total program to purchase through Best Buy. Dishwasher does a good job cleaning. You have the option to control the power of the wash by zones, which is cool if you have pots and pans to wash. The racks that hold the items are all slanted, which sometimes makes it difficult to load the dishwasher with items that do not fit into those rack spaces like mixing bowls or larger storage containers. This dishwasher is very quiet. They have an LED light that shines on the floor to let you know the dishwasher is working. Unless water is draining out into the sink drain, I would have no idea it was even running. The one big negative is the drying capabilities. If you run the normal program, the dishwasher doesn't use heat to dry. The inside of the dishwasher is stainless, and it cools off quicker than the dishes so the condensate forms on the side walls and runs down to drain out. This is okay for anything not plastic, but in our experience anything on the 3rd row is completely wet when the cycle ends (about 2.5 hrs), and anything plastic is still wet. We've tried everything we can, including selecting \"Sanitize\" function, but I would still say it's not great. It's tough to wait 2.5 hours and still have to dry some of the items you're taking out. If the lack of drying doesn't bother you I would recommend getting the Bosch. Otherwise, I would lean towards Kitchenaid.

Sentence (English): Ditched a Samsung that was only 18 months and upgraded to the Bosch.
Comments (English): [ Excellent - But Smells ] || ---------------- || Ditched a Samsung that was only 18 months and upgraded to the Bosch. The Samsung was one problem after the next. The Bosch washes great, easy to use, very quite, fairly spotless drying. No complaints on any of those issues to date. But. It already smells terrible if you close the door after unloading for a day and open it back up. It doesn't take long on a google search to see that folks have been complaining about this for a while now. I did not do that research ahead of time and was convinced by sales person that this is one of the best machine going right now. I'm a former general contractor, have lots of plumbing experience. Everything is installed perfectly. Apparently the pump does not eject all the sump water at the end of the cycle so it just sits there and turns into a cespool very quickly. Very dissapointing that a machine of otherwise amazing quality does not have this addressed. Even my crappy Samsung did that, and even had an auto door opening after dry cycle function. Which this Bosch model does not have. Crazy that that feature is reserved only for the highest end machine. We now use a wooden spoon to hold open the door between loads to keep the thing from stinking up. For the upgrade cost, I would just buy a Miele, except they have no service techs in our area.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher has basically been doing what it's supposed to for the last two weeks and it does it pretty well.
Comments (English): [ Good product - different than expected ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher has basically been doing what it's supposed to for the last two weeks and it does it pretty well. It gets our dishes (4 people in the household, including two small children) very clean and dry. The machine was bought as a replacement for a 12-year-old Bosch SuperSilent dishwasher. The new machine is definitely a little louder than the old one in every conceivable program. If you have a door to the kitchen, you can safely ignore this point. The programs also ALL run longer than on the old machine (which is probably due to the energy and water consumption). The zeolite drying is of course worth mentioning. The drying means that the plastic parts are much drier than on a machine without this feature. Unfortunately, I have to say that our expectations were far from fulfilled. Even with half a load and extra drying and 12 hours of downtime, you still have to wipe with a tea towel (not just on the edges). We will continue testing in the future with programs, filling the machine and other dishwashing additives. The Home Connect connection is actually a useful feature but not absolutely necessary. For people who want to start their dishwasher when they are out and about or want to be reminded when the wash cycle is finished, the app will of course be indispensable. Despite everything, we are very happy with the (not exactly cheap) dishwasher so far, even if it has not quite met our expectations (so far). It will sometimes have to do its job twice a day, and hopefully for as many years as our old machine. We definitely recommend the device so far, even if we could do without some things.
Comments (Original): [ Gutes Produkt - anders als erwartet ] || ---------------- || Die Spülmaschine tut seit 2 Wochen grundsätzlich was sie soll und das ziemlich gut. Sie macht unser Geschirr (4 Personen im Haushalt, davon zwei kleine Kinder) sehr sauber und trocken. Die Maschine wurde als Ersatz für einen 12 Jahre alte Bosch SuperSilent-Spülmaschine gekauft. Die neue Maschine ist auf jeden Fall in jedem erdenklichem Programm ein wenig lauter als die alte. Wer eine Tür zur Küche hat kann diesen Punkt getrost vernachlässigen.Die Programme laufen zudem ALLE länger als bei der alten Maschine (was wahrscheinlich dem Energie-Wasser-Verbrauch geschuldet ist). Erwähnenswert ist natürlich die Zeolith-Trocknung. Die Trocknung schafft es, dass die Plastikteile viel trockener sind als bei einer Maschine ohne diese Einrichtung. Leider muss ich sagen dass unsere Erwartung aber bei Weitem nicht erfüllt wurden. Auch bei halber Beladung und Extra-Trocknen und 12 Stunden Standzeit muss man immer noch mit dem Geschirrtuch nachwischen (nicht nur an den Rändern). Wir werden in Zukunft noch weiter testen mit Programmen, Befüllung der Maschine und anderen Spülzusätzen. Die Home-Connect-Anbindung ist eigentlich auch ein brauchbares Feature aber nicht unbedingt Notwendig. Für Leute die ihren Geschirrspüler von unterwegs starten möchten, oder daran erinnert werden wollen wann der Spülgang fertig ist, wird die App natürlich unerlässlich sein. Bis jetzt sind wir trotz allem sehr zufrieden mit der (nicht ganz günstigen) Spülmaschine, auch wenn sie unsere Erwartung (bis jetzt) noch nicht ganz erfüllt. Sie wird auch manchmal 2x am Tag ihren Dienst verrichten müssen, hoffentlich auch so viel Jahre wie unsere alte Maschine. Wir empfehlen das Gerät auf jeden Fall bisher, auch wenn wir auf manche Sachen auch verzichten könnte.

Sentence (English): Purchased: LG Dios Objet Collection Dishwasher with Hot Air Dryer, Built-in, 12-Person, Nature Beige.
Comments (English): [ I invited an aunt ] || ---------------- || Purchased: LG Dios Objet Collection Dishwasher with Hot Air Dryer, Built-in, 12-Person, Nature Beige. Reason for Purchase: I purchased this to increase the dishwasher capacity to 12. I previously had a 6-person dishwasher, but I gave it away and purchased a 12-person dishwasher. I'll briefly summarize my considerations when purchasing. Why I chose Objet over many other products: The mop base height is crucial when installing a built-in dishwasher. If your mop base is 15cm, Objet is a no-brainer. My mop base is 15cm, which is why I chose Objet. Among all dishwashers with comparable performance, only LG Objet offers 100°C True Steam. While it claims to be able to sterilize baby bottles, I recommend sterilizing them separately. I'm not sure about the importance of a water softener; I haven't noticed any noticeable difference. Water stains can vary significantly depending on the detergent used, so choosing the right detergent is crucial. While it's rated for 12, it doesn't fit all 12 people. One improvement over the 6-person model is that it can also accommodate pots. The hot air drying feature is a double-edged sword. With the hot air drying feature set to full, the dishwasher's run time is three hours, which feels quite long. I don't plan on using it again within three hours, but it still feels a bit long. Other than that, the other functions aren't much different from other dishwashers. The color is a bit beige. It's just beige, a neutral color. My house is installed under an induction stove and uses the same power strip as the induction stove, so I avoid using it simultaneously with the induction stove. Please keep this in mind. The installer was friendly and on time. It must have been difficult, but he did it quickly. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product. If you found my review helpful, please click the "helpful" button. Thank you.
